A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 36-page versions of Advancing Expert Specialization for Better MoE. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–K support reliable comparison; the appendices match in both extracted text and rendered pages.

before.justification: v3.pdf reports original MoE fine-tuning results across 11 benchmarks, loss ablations, and additional sensitivity, architecture, and training-overhead experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v4.pdf retains these original empirical results, including Table 1, Figures 2–4, and the experiments in Appendices H–K.

M1.justification: The objective combination, routing, architecture, and training procedure remain unchanged. Although Equation (6) now explicitly uses stabilized squared projection norms, Appendix C.1 already described these ingredients in v3; the revision corrects the main-text specification of the existing loss.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 11 downstream benchmarks and Numina, GLUE, and FLAN training sources. The mixed Numina–GPQA–HumanEval experiment in Appendix H.3 was already present in v3.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains With Aux Loss, Loss-Free Balancing, GShard, and ST-MoE. Appendix Table 7 retains ERNIE 4.5 LBL and SIMBAL, and the base/AuxOnly/AuxFree comparisons elsewhere are unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated settings remain unchanged, including 6,000 examples per benchmark, three epochs, rank-32 LoRA, and the principal zero-shot evaluation with 512 maximum new tokens. Appendix protocols for longer generation, mixed training data, and additional architectures also match.

E4.justification: The loss ablations and expert/routing analyses in Figures 2–4 are retained. Appendix analyses of loss weights, generation length, training-data diversity, computational overhead, and embedding visualizations are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same ± reporting, and the discussion of averages over multiple measurements is unchanged. Neither version adds run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical testing procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted empirical findings, and appendix results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports the same DeepSeek-V2-Lite/Ours MMLU result of 35.59±0.50. Figure 1 reformats existing empirical displays without changing their reported findings.

T1.justification: Equation (6) replaces the vector-valued expression with squared projection norms and adds epsilon. Equation (8) restores the task-gradient factor, multiplication by the expert output, and the transposed input, while adding stabilization. These are limited mathematical corrections largely aligning the main text with Appendix C; the lemmas and proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: complementary orthogonality and variance objectives, improved specialization and downstream performance, and preserved load balancing without architectural changes. The claimed improvement of up to 23.79% is unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of loss synergy, load balancing, robustness, and computational tradeoffs remain unchanged, as do Section 6's applicability boundaries and future directions. The revised expert-gradient prose reiterates the explanation already present in Appendix C.2.

D1.justification: Hardware, LoRA hyperparameters, loss normalization, inference settings, and the code-access link are unchanged. The denominator stabilizer now shown in the main equations was already documented in Appendix A and Appendix C.1.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 85 reference entries and retain the same related-work discussion and contribution positioning. Reference-page shifts reflect repagination.

P1.justification: The paragraph introducing Equation (8) is locally rewritten, with an explicit explanation of the task-gradient symbol. The author list adds Xinye Cao. Section organization and nearly all other prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 rearranges and resizes its panels and revises its equation annotations. Expanded mathematical material causes local reflow through the main text and references. Other figures and tables retain their designs and content; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the intended scalar loss and expert-gradient factors explicit in Equations (6) and (8), reducing ambiguity and discrepancies with the existing Appendix C explanation. This provides a limited improvement in mathematical clarity; the empirical evidence and proofs are unchanged.
